**Finding: MINCOMMIT — compliant (sits at the fallback).**

- **What exists:** Section 5(a) (p0045) sets a minimum monthly spend for Hosting and Support Services ("but not less than $____ per month"), so this is a genuine take-or-pay floor and the preferred position (no minimum; pay only for usage/ordered Services) is not met.
- **Why it still clears the fallback:** the term is one year (p0078), each auto-renewal is a fresh 12-month term stoppable on 30 days' non-renewal notice, and Section 14 (p0079) gives Client an unconditional election to terminate with the minimums running only to the last day of the following month. There is no shortfall penalty, accelerated minimum or liquidated-damages mechanic anywhere, so there is nothing punitive to convert into a true-up.
- **Noted, not redlined:** the exit is full termination rather than partial reduction and can run to ~59 days rather than exactly 30; no express true-up credit; Section 14's "Subject to Section 4" and Section 6's reference to "minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4" are loose cross-references (the minimums are in Section 5), and Section 6 bars Client from contesting or getting backup for those minimums.
- **Out of scope for this rule:** the credit-report sourcing duty in Section 3(i) is conditional on Client using the Interface, not a volume commitment; the Section 4 support-availability period is a Vendor commitment in our favour.

No redline proposed, consistent with not upgrading a bargain that already meets the fallback.
